newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's cuts rate by 0.25 pct on loans.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's cuts rate by 0.25 pct on loans.

text.p: Morocco's leading Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur on Monday cut its interest rate by 0.25 percent on certain loans to 9.50 percent, a bank spokeswoman said.
"BMCE has cut its interest rate by quarter of a point (1/4) on future loans to enterprises and development projects starting from Monday," the spokeswoman told Reuters.
The interest rate on short term loans was reduced to 9.50 percent from 9.75 percent, she said. She gave no other details.

BMCE's move followed a meeting held by the monetary policy-making national council of money and saving last month during which Finance Minister Mohamed Kabbaj called on the banks to "make an effort and reduce their interest rates...to attract more investments."
BMCE is among Morocco's 18 active banks on the market. It registered a net profit of 259.3 million dirhams ($28.4 million) in the first half of 1996, up 17.7 percent over the same period of 1995.
One of the eight listed banks on the Casablanca stock exchange, BMCE shares were last traded at 420 dirhams.
